To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed novel computational tools to predict the protein structure and function from the sequence, to predict the impact that mutations may have on the protein function, to predict the protein flexibility, to predict the risk of complex and mendelian diseases from exome data, and to predict the blood group from the exome.
we developed new algorithms for protein function and phenotype prediction, that are freely available for research purposes.
we developed new algorithms and models for protein structure prediction and function inference.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of large-scale biological data sets.

the development of novel methods and algorithms for the prediction of protein function and protein structural features, as well as the prediction of genetic diseases and blood groups based on exome sequencing data.
the development of computational methods for protein structure prediction, function prediction, and disease risk assessment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the computational approaches are fundamental to address the next generation sequencing era.
the future of computational biology is bright and promising, and it will be the result of the combination of computer science and biology.
the computational methods proposed in this thesis have shown to be effective in the prediction of protein function and genetic risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the next generation sequencing era is not only a revolution in the way of data collection but also in the way we analyze it.
computational biology is a key discipline to face the challenges of next generation sequencing era.
we are able to predict the function of proteins, the impact of mutations, the risk of diseases, and even the blood group of a person based on the analysis of his genome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of multiple sources of data can be used to predict the function of unknown sequences and to infer the phenotype of an individual based on his genetic variants.
by integrating information from different sources, and by developing predictive models, it is possible to address biological questions that were not possible before the advent of big data.
the integration of different sources of data and information, as well as the development of new algorithms and models are key to address the next generation sequencing era.
